Another problem is the presence of different costs relating to storage, insurance, and cash opportunity costs. These costs affect the management of the physical good. As a result of the disadvantages of direct investment, investors typically prefer to indirectly assume a position in commodity markets to avoid the problems linked to the management of physical goods. These principles are considered to be objective, universal, and immutable, and are often seen as a source of guidance for human behaviour. Natural law theorists believe that the natural world operates according to a set of rational principles, and that these principles can be discovered through human reason and observation. They argue that these principles provide a foundation for moral and legal systems, and that they are binding on all individuals, regardless of their cultural or social background.
